thread:
samuel: Heads-up — we need to settle the "fallback escalation runway" for canary -> fallback transitions. Current problem: short latency spikes cause noisy rollbacks. Want a lightweight proposal to reduce churn and give SREs a predictable escalation path.
ana: +1. Can you sketch the signal flow you imagine?
morgan: One idea: add a short, token-aware dampener window that accumulates anomalous signals and only triggers when they exceed a combined score for N seconds. That avoids flip-flopping on single spikes.
samuel: Exactly. Rough sketch I sent earlier, but here: the combined score = (error_rate zscore * 0.6) + (p95 latency zscore * 0.4) + (user_impact factor). We then require score > threshold for 45s before escalating.
todd: Question: where does this live? Router side or observer? If router-side, we avoid telemetry delay; if observer-side we get richer context. Tradeoff either way.
morgan: Prefer observer-side but paired with a short probe on router to validate before cutoff. So observer raises a candidate escalation, router runs 1-2 quick probes to confirm.
samuel: Probe snippet for sanity check (pseudo):
```
POST /probe/health
{ "variant": "canary", "path": "/v1/generate", "timeout_ms": 200 }
// expect 200 and latency < 250ms for sanity pass
```
ana: Nice. How do we prevent noisy probes from creating more load? Probes must be sampled and rate-limited per-tenant. Also we need opt-out for dedicated/private customers.
oncall-bot: FYI: new runbook will need a breakglass step for urgent customer-impacting rollbacks.
todd: Operationally: 1) observer marks candidate after sustained score, 2) router runs probes (sampled), 3) if confirmed, cut traffic to fallback path with a staged split (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with short hold windows, 4) if rollback required, follow rollback playbook.
morgan: One more thing — add a smoothing TTL: once a tenant experiences an escalation, suppress re-escalation for T minutes unless severity increases. Prevents loops.
samuel: Proposed thresholds and timings to discuss tomorrow: threshold score 2.2, accumulation 45s, probe confirmation within 15s, staged split hold 30s each, suppression TTL 10m. Thoughts?
ana: Those numbers seem reasonable to start. We should add telemetry tags: "escalation.reason","escalation.score","probe.latency_ms","suppression.remaining" for postmortem clarity.
oncall-bot: Added: incident template prefill for escalation events.
morgan: Also recommend a graceful fallback path that downgrades to a narrower model variant rather than full denylist, where possible. Less customer-visible quality delta.
todd: Agree. Add an API flag so product teams can request quality-preserving fallback preference per route.
samuel: Great — I'll draft a short RFC with the sketch, timings, and sample config plus the runbook steps. Ping me if you want to join the RFC sync. :thumbsup:
oncall-bot: deploy-bot scheduled a tiny test rollout for canary-probe infra on 1765630000 (ETA next week).
